chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Aban, from Al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The seven days and the three days in Hajj are not separated; rather, they are at the status of the three days regarding the oath.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: At the status of / Equivalent to

ai.seo_question: How are the days of fasting for expiation of an oath calculated in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith clarifies the flexibility in expiating oaths by equating the seven-day fasting period with the three-day standard, indicating they are interchangeable units rather than rigid, distinct obligations. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that the severity of the expiation can be adapted to the individual's capacity, emphasizing the mercy inherent in the legal dispensation. It underscores the practical application of Quranic verses on oaths, allowing believers to fulfill their religious duties without undue hardship.
